title: The Inch Asked Again

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: An inch is a long way when the hand is small. Ask the pot how far the handle stands; it will tell you the distance and not who set it there.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the drying racks in Low Kiln, in the kiln month

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-ninety-five-to-one-hundred-and-ninety-seven-day-old body carried everywhere and told by nobody — six months and fifteen days to six months and seventeen days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (a cost asked as a direction answered with the pot and the weather, a carried arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, likenesses taken down one at a time before they can stand up and call themselves a rule, and an inch of a small hand going up toward a note and held for the length of a counted breath) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Hand Asked Again
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 195, Ember 16, Sixthday, small hours before first grey through the morning under the Vail kiln-house roof and out into the Clay Yard. Do not recap the close of Chapter 47 and do not re-read the reading. Open on the hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the note of water over water as it did in the night before, and coming down; the count at one hundred and ninety-four is carried into the new morning, exact, complete and unspent, and the boy is one hundred and ninety-five days old and six months and fifteen days and nobody says so (T071/T072). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. The crust lies leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody will perform. The carried fire under the floor gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety-five days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb — three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting, feeds him barley gruel from the house's own dish with two fingers behind his ear, wipes the spoon on her sleeve and not his mouth, tells the carried fire it is the thaw and says The house will keep it (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, for a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1. In the yard a neighbour with a dry scurf of mud on her hem asks what the firing will want now the account has gone up the road; the cost is sent to the pot and the weather and goes away level, nothing priced or entered (T077, T015/T041/T047 held). The sweet edge rides up from High Kiln on a wrong wind and is answered as a direction and not a second edge paid (T064). Then, at the note through the door, the hand goes up an inch and is asked to stay: it holds for the length of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, and comes down against the fold. A physical first asked again and held again, filed on a place of its own — not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment, not one of the three held changes and not a rule; no payer named, nothing promoted (T061/T082). He still cannot close the two inches, lift his chin to the crust or speak a number.

scenes.title: The File Laid Out Again
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 195, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending, heat going first off the high air and staying longest in the low places under the shelf, behind the pot, in the fold of wool. Sella stands with her back to the basket and moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps, the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge so the charcoal tally stays unread, uncounted, uncopied; the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left (T100). She tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot in her hand counting under her breath toward no opening — the small intake, the hold, the letting go — sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and rests her hand a half-beat longer at the setting than the setting needs (T058/T079). At the kindling the small knife lies at the edge of its sill, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, and sweeps the collector's road without turning; no collector comes. His chest is tight since the dark; Ash is worked into his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line; the pale clip-ring holds what light there is; the ear-sentence comes all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath drawn at the top of the reach and not spent; nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled, his stroke over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, knows its note three turns ahead and withholds it from a man on a wrong wind, no pot lost; his bent finger stands in the cold iron while Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot, a remembered repetition and not a change made again, the damper read as one iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies, joined to no kiln (T035/T031/T062). At the going of the light Sella carries him home, going wide around the pan's gone ring, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the empty place in the returning line and the place the carriers crossed; under the roof she sets him on his bed, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen; the two rooms do not touch. In the small hours he lays out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, nine stoppings as objects and not a rule, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the carried man's pale line on a fifth, and now the held inch on a sixth place of its own — each looked at and taken down before any could stand up and call itself a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer (T061/T082, T006, T064). The hand goes up, holds, comes down; one hundred and ninety-five stands exact in the wool.

scenes.title: A Shorter Holding
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 196, Ember 17, Seventhday, before first grey through the morning at the Vail kiln-house, the yard well, the drying racks, the wheel-shed edge and the Clay Yard. The kiln month's second working week runs on without a boundary drawn; the district keeps calling Tallow the firing month and Ember the kiln month and neither is corrected. The boy is one hundred and ninety-six days old and six months and sixteen days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth is still missing with its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety-six days (T088); river, fire and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). Hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath; the kilns stand at their heat. Sella feeds him from the house's own dish, wipes the spoon on her sleeve and not his mouth, gives the instruction to the water, the pot, the broom, the fire and the wool and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar without a touch, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand (T058/T079). At the well a rack woman with slip dried pale in the creases of her wrists asks what the pots will want before the kiln month is out and is told to ask the pot and the weather; a man come off the clay road asks what the kiln will want now the figure has gone up the road and is answered with the house and the weather. Both questions go away level — nothing slopped, priced, refused or entered (T077). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space under the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, the pan's gone round ring with no scrape or chip, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look, a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Before first grey three or four men unnamed go low into the finger's-width-open back room and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T065/T095). Jorra's dust comes out ground small as meal, parted from slip as a surgeon parts a clot from its vessel, the full note known and withheld from a High Kiln kiln-master on a wrong wind, the sweet edge spoken of as a direction with no second edge paid (T035/T031, T064). Mid-morning the hand goes up toward the river's note and comes down before the counted breath has finished — a shorter holding than the day before, the body keeping its own time and the inch no more a reaching for it. Filed where it was filed, not joined, promoted or paired (T061/T082).

scenes.title: What the Dust Did Not Say
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 196, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; the low places keep the heat longest. Sella stands at the shelf with her back to the basket, moves her lips along the row with two gaps and gives nobody a figure, shuts her hand half over the clay jar without touching it, keeps her finger from beneath the front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). A pot set down wrong gives a high thin note before its time; the woman goes on with her hands, sweeps around the fault and makes no lesson of it, and the boy files the note where a danger goes and not among the hearings, not as a seventh and not as a cause (T061/T082, T064 held). At the kindling Tarn tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on; nine stoppings stay nine with no tenth before the seventh year is earned and the loan stays uncalled; his stroke goes over the flagstones and the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). Jorra's bent finger goes into the cold damper while Sella's low unfinished sentence reaches the pot, then the tongue moves a hair's breadth and the finger is left standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again, not stood up with Day 161, 166 or 171; the iron is one piece with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate (T062/T035). The stone lies back in its unmarked clay pot in the Debt Loft, two years gone and cold; from below the boy keeps only the remembering of the small dry scrape of a pot's foot set down on stone, on a place of its own and not made a cause (T006). At the going of the light the basket comes home on the half-pace with the instruction going to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket; the thread is left frozen. In the small hours the file comes back exact, complete and worth nothing: the shorter holding is an object on the sixth place, not a failure, not a sign, not a hearing; the crust, the two shelf gaps, the pan's ring and the field's empty place lie on trays that do not touch, no third gap came and no finger of his drew the line (T060/T086/T097). The hand goes up, holds a little, comes down; one hundred and ninety-six stands unspent.

scenes.title: The Wrong Wind Again
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 197, Ember 18, Eighthday, before first grey through the morning under the Vail roof, at the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the yard well and up and down the clay road. The kiln month's second working week draws toward its end with no boundary drawn. The boy is one hundred and ninety-seven days old and six months and seventeen days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's payer is unnamed for a hundred and ninety-seven days (T088); the other two counts stay in their places and do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool, with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. Sella's instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar without touching it, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, feeds him from the house's own dish and does not wipe his mouth (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, for a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1. Before first grey three or four men unnamed go low into the back room and get no name; Jorra comes through with grey slate dust ground small as meal, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands, tells a pot You'll do, knows the note three turns ahead and withholds it from a man come up on a wrong wind who says a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early — the saying stays a saying about a pot and is not made true as a lesson, no pot lost (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). At the kiln mouth the sweet edge of lead glaze rides up off High Kiln on the wrong wind and goes out on the same wind, a direction spoken of and answered with the pot and the weather; no second edge is paid so soon after the carrying-out, nobody names a cause in Grathic, no collector is called for the glaze-room hand carried out on Day 188 and his pale line stays on its own place (T064). Neighbours asking what the firing will want now the account has gone up the road get the pot and the weather, and the figure gone up in Berr's locked box stays beyond reach with the printed one in twelve unchallenged and the true subtraction inside (T077, T015/T041/T047 held). The yard goes wide around its unswept places and the carriers' place, with a look and no number (T009/T013/T092). Mid-morning the hand goes up toward the note of water over water and comes down at once, with no holding in it on this morning — the asking is not always answered and an inch is still worth nothing; filed on its own place and not made into a rule (T061/T082).

scenes.title: Held Into the Letting Go
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 197, Ember 18, Eighthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending, going off the high air first and staying longest under the shelf, behind the pot, in the fold of wool where the boy lies. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along the row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, keeps her finger from beneath the front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands with the back of the pot in her hand counting under her breath toward no opening — the small intake at the top, the hold, the letting go — pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out on the board with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling the knife lies at the edge of its sill with six counted in the worn thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on; nine stoppings stand as objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled, his stroke over the bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra gives the men no name, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells the wheel and the pot their sayings, withholds the note from the wrong wind, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper until Sella's sentence reaches the pot — a remembered repetition, not a change made again; he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates stays ungiven (T035/T031/T062). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road with woodsmoke before her in long low bars and the river wind behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed; under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, banks the coals with the back of a broken pot and does not touch the widow's mark, because a dusk is not an opening and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1. In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel, each thing in its own hollow: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh; three near-full answers advanced and unpaid; nine stoppings with no tenth; three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth and the pale line on a fifth; the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid; the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's gone ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch; no third gap, no fourth likeness and no finger drawn across them (T061/T082, T060/T086/T097). Then the hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and does not come down at once. It stays up through the whole of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch this one — the small intake at the top, the hold, and on into the letting go — and comes down with the breath rather than before it, against the fold. The longest holding yet, held into the letting go and let go with it: an inch of a small soft hand, a physical first asked three times in three days, filed on a place of its own and never laid across the others; not a reaching, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment, not one of the three held changes, not a key, not a power and not a rule, with no payer named and no doctrine stood up out of it (T061/T082). He still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift his chin to the crust or speak a number. One hundred and ninety-seven stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody; the fire's fifth has had no payer for a hundred and ninety-seven days, the charcoal waits under the shelf, the mark hangs untouched, the stone lies cold in its loft pot, the Seed 16 breath is unspent and the loan uncalled, and the cost of the man carried out stands entered nowhere. The three counts keep their three places and do not become one. Forward, not closed: the count goes into Day 198, Ember 19, and the second Account-day and market of Ember stands two days off.
